args.content:
# direnv v2.37.1 — misc commands & configuration specification

Behavioral specification of: `version`, `help` / no-args / unknown commands, `edit`,
`log`, `fetchurl`, and configuration-file loading (incl. `whitelist`, `log_format`,
`log_filter`). Derived purely from black-box probing of the reference binary.

Conventions used below:

- `ESC` = byte 0x1b. All colored stderr messages are emitted with ANSI escapes
  **unconditionally** — colors do NOT depend on tty, TERM, or piping (verified with
  piped stderr, a pty via `script(1)`, and `TERM=dumb`; identical bytes in all cases).
- Every error line has the form `ESC[31mdirenv: error <msg>ESC[0m\n` (red), and every
  status line the form `ESC[0mdirenv: <msg>\n` (note: leading reset, no trailing reset).
- Exit codes: success = 0, any command failure = 1 (no other codes observed, even when a
  child process exits 127 — direnv still exits 1).

---

## 1. `direnv version [VERSION_AT_LEAST]`

### No arguments

- stdout (exact bytes): `2.37.1\n`
- stderr: empty
- exit code: 0

`direnv --version` behaves identically. (`-version` is an unknown command, see §2.)

### With VERSION_AT_LEAST

stdout is always empty. Exit 0 iff the running version `2.37.1` is **greater than or
equal to** the argument, else exit 1 with an error on stderr.

**Normalization/validation algorithm** (matches `golang.org/x/mod/semver` exactly):

1. If the argument does not start with `v`, a single `v` is prepended (only for
   validation, comparison, and error messages; `v2.37.1` and `2.37.1` are equivalent).
2. The result must be valid per x/mod/semver `IsValid`:
   `vMAJOR[.MINOR[.PATCH]][-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]` where MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH are decimal
   numbers **without leading zeroes**, PRERELEASE is dot-separated identifiers of
   `[0-9A-Za-z-]` (numeric identifiers also without leading zeroes), BUILD is ignored.
   Two- and one-part versions are valid (`2.37`, `2`, `0` all valid).
3. Comparison is x/mod/semver `Compare` (numeric major/minor/patch, prerelease < release,
   prerelease identifiers compared numerically/lexically per semver, build ignored).

Observed verdicts (current = `2.37.1`):

| arg | result | | arg | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2.37.1`, `v2.37.1` | exit 0 (equal) | | `2.37.2`, `2.38`, `3.0`, `v2.38` | exit 1 (older) |
| `2.37.0`, `2.37`, `2.36`, `2`, `1.99.99`, `0` | exit 0 | | `2.37.10`, `2.370` | exit 1 (older) |
| `2.37.1-rc1`, `2.37.1-rc.2`, `2.37.1-alpha.1` | exit 0 (release ≥ its prereleases) | | `2.37.2-rc.1` | exit 1 (older) |
| `2.37.1+build` | exit 0 (build ignored) | | `999999999999999999999999` | exit 1 (valid, huge, older) |
| `""`, `garbage`, `vfoo`, `v`, `2.x.1`, `-1`, `2.37.1.0`, `02.37.1`, `2.037.1`, ` 2.37.1`, `2.37.1 `, `2.37.1\n` (literal backslash-n), `2. 37.1`, `2.37.1-01`, `2.37.1-`, `2.37.1-alpha..1`, `2.37.1-a_b`, `vv2.37.1`, `--help` | exit 1 (invalid semver) | | | |

**Error messages** (stderr, exit 1; `<v+arg>` = argument with exactly one leading `v`
ensured — the raw argument is echoed, prepending `v` only if absent):

- Invalid: `ESC[31mdirenv: error vgarbage is not a valid semver versionESC[0m\n`
  (for arg `garbage`; arg `vv2.37.1` → `...error vv2.37.1 is not a valid semver version...`;
  arg `""` → `...error v is not a valid semver version...`)
- Older: `ESC[31mdirenv: error current version v2.37.1 is older than the desired version v2.37.2ESC[0m\n`
  (for arg `2.37.2`; the current version is always printed as `v2.37.1`)

Extra arguments are ignored: `direnv version 2.37.1 extra-arg` → exit 0.
There is no flag parsing; `--help` is treated as a version string.

> Not determinable from one binary: whether `2.37` compares equal to `2.37.0`
> (untestable with a fixed current version 2.37.1; assume x/mod/semver semantics, where
> missing minor/patch are not equal to explicit ones for `Compare` — `v2.37 < v2.37.0`).

---

## 2. `direnv help`, no-args, and unknown commands

### `direnv` (no arguments)

Identical to `direnv help`: prints the public help to **stdout**, exit 0, empty stderr.

### `direnv help [SHOW_PRIVATE]`

- `direnv help` → public help on stdout, exit 0. Byte-for-byte content is in
  `/workspace/reference/assets/help.txt` (1258 bytes) **except** the line
  `  Supported SHELL values are: [...]` (line 19): the 12 shell names
  (`bash, elvish, fish, gha, gzenv, json, murex, pwsh, systemd, tcsh, vim, zsh`) are
  printed in a **random order on every invocation** (Go map iteration order; three runs
  gave three different orders). The brackets and `, ` separator are literal:
  `Supported SHELL values are: [fish, gzenv, json, ...]`.
- `direnv help <arg>` where **any argument is non-empty** (even `false`, `garbage`, `1`,
  `TRUE`) → prints the *private* help (2169 bytes), exit 0; content is
  `/workspace/reference/assets/help_private.txt` modulo the same randomized shell-order
  line (line 29). Private help lists extra commands prefixed with `* ` and ends with
  the line `* = private commands\n`.
- `direnv help ""` → public help (empty string counts as "no argument").
  `direnv help "" true` → private help.
- `direnv --help` → public help, exit 0.
- All help output goes to stdout only; stderr is always empty; exit is always 0.

### Unknown command

`direnv garbagecmd` (also `-h`, `-version`, any unrecognized first arg):

- stdout: empty
- stderr: `ESC[31mdirenv: error command "<argv0> <cmd>" not foundESC[0m\n`
- exit code: 1

`<argv0>` is the command path **as invoked** (e.g. `/workspace/executable garbagecmd`
when invoked by full path; would be `direnv garbagecmd` when found via PATH). Only
argv[0] and argv[1] appear in the message: `direnv foo bar baz` still prints
`command "/workspace/executable foo" not found`.

---

## 3. `direnv edit [PATH_TO_RC]`

Opens an rc file in `$EDITOR` and (conditionally) allows it afterwards.

### Target resolution

- No argument: searches from CWD **upward** for an `.envrc` (or `.env` when
  `[global] load_dotenv = true`). If found, the **absolute** path is edited.
  If nothing is found:
  - stderr: `ESC[31mdirenv: error .envrc or .env not found. Use \`direnv edit .\` to create a new .envrc in the current directoryESC[0m\n`
  - exit 1, editor is NOT run.
- Argument is an **existing directory**: edits `<arg>/.envrc` (arg used verbatim —
  `edit .` → `.envrc` relative; `edit sub1` → `sub1/.envrc`; `edit /abs/dir` → absolute).
  The file need not exist; direnv does **not** create it — the editor is expected to.
- Any other argument (nonexistent dir, plain filename, explicit `.envrc` path): used
  **verbatim** as the file path (`edit nope.txt` → `nope.txt`, `edit nodir` → `nodir`).
- Extra arguments are silently ignored (`edit . extra` edits `.envrc`).

### Editor invocation

- Uses `$EDITOR` only. `$VISUAL` is **ignored** entirely.
- If `EDITOR` is unset or empty:
  - stderr line 1: `ESC[31mdirenv: $EDITOR not found.ESC[0m\n` (red, but no `error ` prefix)
  - then direnv searches PATH for a fallback editor, in this priority order
    (first found wins): **`editor` > `subl` > `nano` > `vim` > `emacs`**.
    (`vi`, `nvim`, `sensible-editor`, `code`, `atom`, `gedit`, `kak`, `micro`, `hx`,
    `pico`, `joe` are NOT tried.)
  - If none found: stderr line 2: `ESC[31mdirenv: error could not find a default editor in the PATHESC[0m\n`, exit 1.
- The editor is run through bash as: `<bash_path> -c '<EDITOR> <bash-quoted-path>'`
  where `bash_path` is the configured/found bash (`/usr/bin/bash` here) and the path is
  quoted with Bash ANSI-C quoting (`$'...'`). Observed literally:
  `bash -c "/tmp/probe_misc/editor.sh \$'/tmp/probe_misc/proj/.envrc'"`.
  Consequences: `$EDITOR` is **shell-interpreted** — `EDITOR="myeditor --some flag"`
  works (editor receives `--some`, `flag`, `<path>` as 3 args), and shell syntax in
  EDITOR (e.g. `EDITOR='echo x > f; vim'`) is executed. Paths containing spaces arrive
  as a single argument.
- Editor failure: direnv prints `ESC[31mdirenv: error exit status <n>ESC[0m\n` and exits
  **1** regardless of n (editor exit 3 → `error exit status 3`, direnv exit 1; nonexistent
  editor → bash prints its own `line 1: ...: No such file or directory`, then
  `error exit status 127`, direnv exit 1). No allow happens on editor failure.
- Editor success (exit 0): direnv exit 0, no output (stdout/stderr empty), even if the
  target file was never created.

### Auto-allow after editing (verified, non-obvious semantics)

The allow decision is based on the **RC file found from the current working directory**
(the same upward search as no-arg resolution), *not* on the file being edited:

1. Before launching the editor, direnv records the found-RC path and its mtime
   (or "none" if no RC exists).
2. After the editor exits 0, it re-resolves and re-stats the found RC.
3. If the found RC **changed in any way** — different path, different mtime, newly
   appeared, or deleted — then direnv allows **the edited file** (writes
   `$XDG_DATA_HOME/direnv/allow/<sha256>` containing the edited file's absolute path;
   hash = sha256 of `abspath + "\n" + contents`, as for `direnv allow`).
   Otherwise nothing is allowed.

Verified cases (CWD = `/tmp/probe/misc/proj` containing `.envrc`):

- `edit .`, editor rewrites/touches `./.envrc` → `./.envrc` allowed.
- `edit .` or no-arg, editor does nothing → NOT allowed.
- no-arg `edit`, editor only `touch`es the rc (same content) → allowed (mtime is what matters).
- `edit sub1/.envrc`, editor rewrites `sub1/.envrc` only → **NOT** allowed (CWD rc untouched).
- `edit sub1/.envrc`, editor only touches `./.envrc` → `sub1/.envrc` IS allowed.
- `edit sub2` (empty dir), editor creates `sub2/.envrc` → NOT allowed.
- `edit <newfile>` in a directory tree with no rc anywhere → NOT allowed.
- editor deletes the CWD rc → edited file allowed ("changed" includes deletion).
- In a CWD with no rc at all, `edit .` where the editor creates `./.envrc` → allowed
  (found RC went from none → `./.envrc`).

---

## 4. `direnv log (--status|--error) <message>`

Argument rules (checked in this order):

1. Exactly 2 arguments required (after `log`); otherwise
   `ESC[31mdirenv: error invalid argumentsESC[0m\n`, exit 1.
   (`log`, `log ""`, `log hello`, `log --status`, `log --status a b` all → this error.)
2. Argument 1 must be exactly `--status`, `-status`, `--error`, or `-error`
   (single-dash variants accepted; `status`, `--STATUS`, `---status`, `--`,
   `--status=x` rejected). Otherwise:
   `ESC[31mdirenv: error invalid log-type '<arg>'ESC[0m\n`, exit 1.
3. Argument 2 is the message, printed **verbatim** (embedded newlines/tabs/unicode pass
   through; empty string allowed).

Output (stderr only, stdout always empty, exit 0):

- `log --status hello` → `ESC[0mdirenv: hello\n`
- `log --error hello` → `ESC[31mdirenv: helloESC[0m\n`
- `log --status ""` → `ESC[0mdirenv: \n` ; `log --error ""` → `ESC[31mdirenv: ESC[0m\n`
- Multi-line: `log --status $'line1\nline2'` → `ESC[0mdirenv: line1\nline2\n`

### Interaction with `[global] log_format` / `log_filter` (see §6)

These knobs apply **only to `--status`**; `--error` always uses the default
`direnv: %s` format and is never filtered:

- Default status format is `direnv: %s`. `log_format = "CUSTOM:%s"` →
  `ESC[0mCUSTOM:hi\n`. `log_format = "-"` → status message suppressed entirely
  (zero bytes). `log_format = ""` → treated as unset (default used).
- The format string is applied **twice** through Go's `fmt.Sprintf`:
  output = `Sprintf(Sprintf(log_format, msg))` + `\n`. With a format lacking `%s`
  this produces Go's `%!`-artifacts, e.g. `log_format = "no-percent"` yields exactly
  `ESC[0mno-percent\n%!!(MISSING)(EXTRA string=hi)\n`, and `log_format = "%s %s"`
  yields `ESC[0mhi %!!(MISSING)s(MISSING)\n`.
- `log_filter` is a **keep-only** regexp on the formatted status message (not a
  drop filter): `log_filter = "hi"` keeps `hi there` (prints) and suppresses `bye`.
  Errors are unaffected (`log --error bye` still prints).
- Invalid regexp: each status-log attempt prints
  `ESC[31mdirenv: error error in log filter: error parsing regexp: missing closing ]: \`[\`ESC[0m\n`
  (for filter `[`) — note the doubled `error error in`.

---

## 5. `direnv fetchurl <url> [<integrity-hash>]`

Fetches a URL into a content-addressed store (CAS).

### CAS layout

- Directory: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/direnv/cas/` (created `0755`; if `XDG_CACHE_HOME` unset or
  empty: `$HOME/.cache/direnv/cas/`).
- File name: the **lowercase hex** encoding of the hash digest (NOT the SRI/base64 form
  shown in the man page — the man page is outdated). For sha256: 64 hex chars, e.g.
  `…/cas/23e4ca4c602ddb27746ab41722b4dfa5466299d4afe2634943254a5a29c5e485`.
- Cached files are mode **`0500`** (`r-x------`): read-only + executable for owner.
- Downloads go to a temp file `…/cas/tmp<random-number>` which is renamed into place.

### Mode 1: URL only — discover the hash

- Always performs an HTTP GET (even if the content is already in the CAS).
- Computes the **sha256** of the response body. If the CAS file for it does not exist,
  it is stored (rename, mode 0500); if it exists, nothing is stored.
- stdout when **not a tty** (piped/redirected): exactly `sha256-<base64std-padded>\n`, e.g.
  `sha256-I+TKTGAt2yd0arQXIrTfpUZimdSv4mNJQyVKWinF5IU=\n`
- stdout when **a tty** (human-readable, `\n` line endings):
  ```
  Found hash: sha256-<hash>

  Invoke fetchurl again with the hash as an argument to get the disk location:

    direnv fetchurl "<url>" "sha256-<hash>"
    #=> <absolute-cas-path>
  ```
- stderr: on a fresh store-into-CAS, two quirky warnings are printed (plain text, no
  colors/prefix; tmp name varies):
  ```
  Warning: failed to close temp file: close <casdir>/tmp<num>: file already closed
  Warning: failed to remove temp file <casdir>/tmp<num>: remove <casdir>/tmp<num>: no such file or directory
  ```
  On a cache-warm URL-only call, no warnings. Exit 0.

### Mode 2: URL + integrity hash

- Hash syntax: `<algo>-<base64>` (SRI-like). Algo `sha256`, `sha384`, `sha512` parse;
  anything else → `ESC[31mdirenv: error sri: unsupported algo <algo>ESC[0m\n`, exit 1
  (observed for `md5`, `sha1`). A string without `-` →
  `ESC[31mdirenv: error sri: not a hash <arg>ESC[0m\n`, exit 1. Standard padded base64
  required: malformed → e.g. `ESC[31mdirenv: error illegal base64 data at input byte 0ESC[0m\n`
  (byte offset varies), exit 1.
- **Cache check first**: if `<casdir>/<hex-of-given-hash-digest>` exists, the path is
  printed and the command exits 0 — **no network request and no content verification**
  (verified: pre-seeding the file with wrong content still succeeds; a `sha384-…` hash
  can only ever succeed this way, since the downloaded digest is always sha256).
- Otherwise: HTTP GET, compute **sha256** of the body, compare against the given hash
  (as full `algo-base64` strings):
  - match → store in CAS (rename + the two temp-file warnings), stdout =
    `<absolute-cas-path>\n`, exit 0.
  - mismatch → nothing stored, stdout empty, exit 1:
    `ESC[31mdirenv: error hash mismatch. Expected '<given-hash>' but got 'sha256-<actual>'ESC[0m\n`
    (e.g. `Expected 'sha256-' but got …` for an empty-digest hash; a `sha512-…` or
    `sha384-…` given hash always mismatches because "got" is always `sha256-…`).
- Extra arguments are ignored.

### HTTP behavior / errors (all exit 1, stdout empty, `ESC[31mdirenv: error …ESC[0m\n`)

- Missing URL: `… error missing URL argument …`
- Redirects (301 etc.) are followed (verified: `/subdir` → 301 → `/subdir/` → 200).
- Non-200 final status: `… error expected status code 200 but got 404 …`
- Bad URL `notaurl`: `… error Get "notaurl": unsupported protocol scheme "" …`
- Bad URL `://bad`: `… error parse "://bad": missing protocol scheme …`
- `ftp://…`: `… error Get "ftp://example.com/x": unsupported protocol scheme "ftp" …`
- Connection refused (server down): `… error Get "<url>": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:<port>: connect: connection refused …`
  — note a warm cache still errors **if the URL is fetched**; but in URL+hash mode a
  cache hit never touches the network, so it succeeds with the server down.

---

## 6. Configuration file loading

### Locations and precedence

- Config directory = `$DIRENV_CONFIG` if that env var is **non-empty**, else
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/direnv` if `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` non-empty, else `$HOME/.config/direnv`.
  - `DIRENV_CONFIG` pointing to a nonexistent directory, or to a regular file, is
    treated as "no config" silently (no error).
  - If no config directory can be determined at all (HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME both
    unset), commands that need the config fail with
    `ESC[31mdirenv: error couldn't find a configuration directory for direnvESC[0m\n`,
    exit 1 (observed for `status`, `edit`, `log`; `version` still works, exit 0).
- Inside the config directory, the file **`direnv.toml`** is read. If `direnv.toml`
  does not exist, the legacy **`config.toml`** is read instead. If **both** exist,
  `direnv.toml` wins completely (verified: whitelist in `config.toml` ignored when a
  `direnv.toml` without whitelist is present). If neither exists, defaults are used
  silently.
- Unknown TOML sections/keys are ignored (exit 0).
- Malformed TOML, or type mismatches, abort the whole command: stdout empty, exit 1:
  - `ESC[31mdirenv: error LoadConfig() failed to parse <path>: toml: line 2: expected '.' or ']' to end table name, but got '\n' insteadESC[0m\n` (for `[whitelist` + `prefix = [`)
  - `ESC[31mdirenv: error LoadConfig() failed to parse <path>: toml: line 2 (last key "whitelist.prefix"): incompatible types: TOML value has type string; destination has type sliceESC[0m\n` (for `prefix = "..."` instead of an array; same for `prefix = [ 123 ]` with type int)
  - `ESC[31mdirenv: error LoadConfig() failed to parse <path>: toml: line 1 (last key "x"): expected value but found '\n' insteadESC[0m\n` (for `x = `)
  (Error text is from the pelletier/go-toml v2 parser.)

### `[whitelist]` — implicit allow

`prefix` and `exact` each accept an array of strings. A whitelisted `.envrc` is loaded
by `direnv export <shell>` (and other loading commands) **without `direnv allow`** —
verified: export exits 0 and emits the usual status lines
(`ESC[0mdirenv: loading <path>\n`, `ESC[0mdirenv: export +VAR\n`).
Without whitelist/allow the same export exits 1 with stdout still containing the
`DIRENV_*` export statements and stderr:
`ESC[31mdirenv: error <abspath>/.envrc is blocked. Run \`direnv allow\` to approve its contentESC[0m\n`.

Tilde expansion: an entry starting with `~/` has the `~` replaced by `$HOME`
(`~/wlproj`, `~/`, `~/wlproj/.envrc` all work). A bare `~` is NOT expanded.

`prefix` — **pure string-prefix match** on the `.envrc`'s absolute path (after tilde
expansion). No path cleaning, no component awareness:

- `prefix = ["/tmp/probe_misc/wl"]` allows `/tmp/probe_misc/wl/proj/.envrc` **and also**
  `/tmp/probe_misc/wl2/proj/.envrc` (shares the string prefix!).
- Partial components match: `prefix = ["/tmp/probe_misc/w"]` allows `…/wl/proj/.envrc`.
- Trailing slash is fine (`…/wl/` matches).
- Double slashes do NOT match (`/tmp//probe_misc//wl` ≠ the real path).
- Relative entries never match (paths compared are absolute).
- `prefix = [""]` matches everything.

`exact` — exact string match after normalization:

- An entry that is a directory path is treated as `<entry>/.envrc`
  (docs; verified: `exact = ["/tmp/probe_misc/wl/proj"]` allows exactly
  `/tmp/probe_misc/wl/proj/.envrc`).
- A full file path (`…/proj/.envrc`) also works. A trailing slash on a directory entry
  still works (`…/proj/`), but a trailing slash on a file entry (`…/proj/.envrc/`)
  does NOT match.
- Does not extend to nested directories: with `exact = ["…/wl/proj"]`,
  `…/wl/proj/nested/.envrc` is still blocked.
- Non-matching paths are simply blocked (no error).

### `[global] log_format` / `log_filter`

Covered in §4 (they affect status logging, incl. `direnv log --status`; defaults:
`log_format = "direnv: %s"`, no filter; `log_format = "-"` disables status logs).

---

## 7. Things I could NOT determine

1. `version` comparison of two- vs three-part equality (`2.37` vs `2.37.0`) — untestable
   with a fixed binary version of 2.37.1; assumed `golang.org/x/mod/semver` semantics.
2. The exact set/order of fallback editors beyond what PATH probing revealed
   (`editor > subl > nano > vim > emacs`); an exotic default editor present on some
   other system can't be ruled out, but these five are the complete accepted set among
   15 common names tested.
3. fetchurl with `sha384`/`sha512` given hashes: the cache-hit filename uses the hex of
   the given digest, but a cache *miss* can never succeed (computed digest is always
   sha256, so the string comparison always fails) — whether this is intentional or a
   bug is not observable.
4. Whether the two fetchurl temp-file warnings (close/remove) are version- or
   OS-dependent; observed consistently on this Linux ext4-ish /tmp.
5. `log_filter` matching is applied to the formatted message string; whether it also
   sees the `direnv: ` prefix or ANSI bytes was not fully pinned down (filter `hi`
   matched message `hi there`; filter on the prefix text was not tested).

display.content:
# direnv v2.37.1 — misc commands & configuration specification

Behavioral specification of: `version`, `help` / no-args / unknown commands, `edit`,
`log`, `fetchurl`, and configuration-file loading (incl. `whitelist`, `log_format`,
`log_filter`). Derived purely from black-box probing of the reference binary.

Conventions used below:

- `ESC` = byte 0x1b. All colored stderr messages are emitted with ANSI escapes
  **unconditionally** — colors do NOT depend on tty, TERM, or piping (verified with
  piped stderr, a pty via `script(1)`, and `TERM=dumb`; identical bytes in all cases).
- Every error line has the form `ESC[31mdirenv: error <msg>ESC[0m\n` (red), and every
  status line the form `ESC[0mdirenv: <msg>\n` (note: leading reset, no trailing reset).
- Exit codes: success = 0, any command failure = 1 (no other codes observed, even when a
  child process exits 127 — direnv still exits 1).

---

## 1. `direnv version [VERSION_AT_LEAST]`

### No arguments

- stdout (exact bytes): `2.37.1\n`
- stderr: empty
- exit code: 0

`direnv --version` behaves identically. (`-version` is an unknown command, see §2.)

### With VERSION_AT_LEAST

stdout is always empty. Exit 0 iff the running version `2.37.1` is **greater than or
equal to** the argument, else exit 1 with an error on stderr.

**Normalization/validation algorithm** (matches `golang.org/x/mod/semver` exactly):

1. If the argument does not start with `v`, a single `v` is prepended (only for
   validation, comparison, and error messages; `v2.37.1` and `2.37.1` are equivalent).
2. The result must be valid per x/mod/semver `IsValid`:
   `vMAJOR[.MINOR[.PATCH]][-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]` where MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH are decimal
   numbers **without leading zeroes**, PRERELEASE is dot-separated identifiers of
   `[0-9A-Za-z-]` (numeric identifiers also without leading zeroes), BUILD is ignored.
   Two- and one-part versions are valid (`2.37`, `2`, `0` all valid).
3. Comparison is x/mod/semver `Compare` (numeric major/minor/patch, prerelease < release,
   prerelease identifiers compared numerically/lexically per semver, build ignored).

Observed verdicts (current = `2.37.1`):

| arg | result | | arg | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2.37.1`, `v2.37.1` | exit 0 (equal) | | `2.37.2`, `2.38`, `3.0`, `v2.38` | exit 1 (older) |
| `2.37.0`, `2.37`, `2.36`, `2`, `1.99.99`, `0` | exit 0 | | `2.37.10`, `2.370` | exit 1 (older) |
| `2.37.1-rc1`, `2.37.1-rc.2`, `2.37.1-alpha.1` | exit 0 (release ≥ its prereleases) | | `2.37.2-rc.1` | exit 1 (older) |
| `2.37.1+build` | exit 0 (build ignored) | | `999999999999999999999999` | exit 1 (valid, huge, older) |
| `""`, `garbage`, `vfoo`, `v`, `2.x.1`, `-1`, `2.37.1.0`, `02.37.1`, `2.037.1`, ` 2.37.1`, `2.37.1 `, `2.37.1\n` (literal backslash-n), `2. 37.1`, `2.37.1-01`, `2.37.1-`, `2.37.1-alpha..1`, `2.37.1-a_b`, `vv2.37.1`, `--help` | exit 1 (invalid semver) | | | |

**Error messages** (stderr, exit 1; `<v+arg>` = argument with exactly one leading `v`
ensured — the raw argument is echoed, prepending `v` only if absent):

- Invalid: `ESC[31mdirenv: error vgarbage is not a valid semver versionESC[0m\n`
  (for arg `garbage`; arg `vv2.37.1` → `...error vv2.37.1 is not a valid semver version...`;
  arg `""` → `...error v is not a valid semver version...`)
- Older: `ESC[31mdirenv: error current version v2.37.1 is older than the desired version v2.37.2ESC[0m\n`
  (for arg `2.37.2`; the current version is always printed as `v2.37.1`)

Extra arguments are ignored: `direnv version 2.37.1 extra-arg` → exit 0.
There is no flag parsing; `--help` is treated as a version string.

> Not determinable from one binary: whether `2.37` compares equal to `2.37.0`
> (untestable with a fixed current version 2.37.1; assume x/mod/semver semantics, where
> missing minor/patch are not equal to explicit ones for `Compare` — `v2.37 < v2.37.0`).

---

## 2. `direnv help`, no-args, and unknown commands

### `direnv` (no arguments)

Identical to `direnv help`: prints the public help to **stdout**, exit 0, empty stderr.

### `direnv help [SHOW_PRIVATE]`

- `direnv help` → public help on stdout, exit 0. Byte-for-byte content is in
  `/workspace/reference/assets/help.txt` (1258 bytes) **except** the line
  `  Supported SHELL values are: [...]` (line 19): the 12 shell names
  (`bash, elvish, fish, gha, gzenv, json, murex, pwsh, systemd, tcsh, vim, zsh`) are
  printed in a **random order on every invocation** (Go map iteration order; three runs
  gave three different orders). The brackets and `, ` separator are literal:
  `Supported SHELL values are: [fish, gzenv, json, ...]`.
- `direnv help <arg>` where **any argument is non-empty** (even `false`, `garbage`, `1`,
  `TRUE`) → prints the *private* help (2169 bytes), exit 0; content is
  `/workspace/reference/assets/help_private.txt` modulo the same randomized shell-order
  line (line 29). Private help lists extra commands prefixed with `* ` and ends with
  the line `* = private commands\n`.
- `direnv help ""` → public help (empty string counts as "no argument").
  `direnv help "" true` → private help.
- `direnv --help` → public help, exit 0.
- All help output goes to stdout only; stderr is always empty; exit is always 0.

### Unknown command

`direnv garbagecmd` (also `-h`, `-version`, any unrecognized first arg):

- stdout: empty
- stderr: `ESC[31mdirenv: error command "<argv0> <cmd>" not foundESC[0m\n`
- exit code: 1

`<argv0>` is the command path **as invoked** (e.g. `/workspace/executable garbagecmd`
when invoked by full path; would be `direnv garbagecmd` when found via PATH). Only
argv[0] and argv[1] appear in the message: `direnv foo bar baz` still prints
`command "/workspace/executable foo" not found`.

---

## 3. `direnv edit [PATH_TO_RC]`

Opens an rc file in `$EDITOR` and (conditionally) allows it afterwards.

### Target resolution

- No argument: searches from CWD **upward** for an `.envrc` (or `.env` when
  `[global] load_dotenv = true`). If found, the **absolute** path is edited.
  If nothing is found:
  - stderr: `ESC[31mdirenv: error .envrc or .env not found. Use \`direnv edit .\` to create a new .envrc in the current directoryESC[0m\n`
  - exit 1, editor is NOT run.
- Argument is an **existing directory**: edits `<arg>/.envrc` (arg used verbatim —
  `edit .` → `.envrc` relative; `edit sub1` → `sub1/.envrc`; `edit /abs/dir` → absolute).
  The file need not exist; direnv does **not** create it — the editor is expected to.
- Any other argument (nonexistent dir, plain filename, explicit `.envrc` path): used
  **verbatim** as the file path (`edit nope.txt` → `nope.txt`, `edit nodir` → `nodir`).
- Extra arguments are silently ignored (`edit . extra` edits `.envrc`).

### Editor invocation

- Uses `$EDITOR` only. `$VISUAL` is **ignored** entirely.
- If `EDITOR` is unset or empty:
  - stderr line 1: `ESC[31mdirenv: $EDITOR not found.ESC[0m\n` (red, but no `error ` prefix)
  - then direnv searches PATH for a fallback editor, in this priority order
    (first found wins): **`editor` > `subl` > `nano` > `vim` > `emacs`**.
    (`vi`, `nvim`, `sensible-editor`, `code`, `atom`, `gedit`, `kak`, `micro`, `hx`,
    `pico`, `joe` are NOT tried.)
  - If none found: stderr line 2: `ESC[31mdirenv: error could not find a default editor in the PATHESC[0m\n`, exit 1.
- The editor is run through bash as: `<bash_path> -c '<EDITOR> <bash-quoted-path>'`
  where `bash_path` is the configured/found bash (`/usr/bin/bash` here) and the path is
  quoted with Bash ANSI-C quoting (`$'...'`). Observed literally:
  `bash -c "/tmp/probe_misc/editor.sh \$'/tmp/probe_misc/proj/.envrc'"`.
  Consequences: `$EDITOR` is **shell-interpreted** — `EDITOR="myeditor --some flag"`
  works (editor receives `--some`, `flag`, `<path>` as 3 args), and shell syntax in
  EDITOR (e.g. `EDITOR='echo x > f; vim'`) is executed. Paths containing spaces arrive
  as a single argument.
- Editor failure: direnv prints `ESC[31mdirenv: error exit status <n>ESC[0m\n` and exits
  **1** regardless of n (editor exit 3 → `error exit status 3`, direnv exit 1; nonexistent
  editor → bash prints its own `line 1: ...: No such file or directory`, then
  `error exit status 127`, direnv exit 1). No allow happens on editor failure.
- Editor success (exit 0): direnv exit 0, no output (stdout/stderr empty), even if the
  target file was never created.

### Auto-allow after editing (verified, non-obvious semantics)

The allow decision is based on the **RC file found from the current working directory**
(the same upward search as no-arg resolution), *not* on the file being edited:

1. Before launching the editor, direnv records the found-RC path and its mtime
   (or "none" if no RC exists).
2. After the editor exits 0, it re-resolves and re-stats the found RC.
3. If the found RC **changed in any way** — different path, different mtime, newly
   appeared, or deleted — then direnv allows **the edited file** (writes
   `$XDG_DATA_HOME/direnv/allow/<sha256>` containing the edited file's absolute path;
   hash = sha256 of `abspath + "\n" + contents`, as for `direnv allow`).
   Otherwise nothing is allowed.

Verified cases (CWD = `/tmp/probe/misc/proj` containing `.envrc`):

- `edit .`, editor rewrites/touches `./.envrc` → `./.envrc` allowed.
- `edit .` or no-arg, editor does nothing → NOT allowed.
- no-arg `edit`, editor only `touch`es the rc (same content) → allowed (mtime is what matters).
- `edit sub1/.envrc`, editor rewrites `sub1/.envrc` only → **NOT** allowed (CWD rc untouched).
- `edit sub1/.envrc`, editor only touches `./.envrc` → `sub1/.envrc` IS allowed.
- `edit sub2` (empty dir), editor creates `sub2/.envrc` → NOT allowed.
- `edit <newfile>` in a directory tree with no rc anywhere → NOT allowed.
- editor deletes the CWD rc → edited file allowed ("changed" includes deletion).
- In a CWD with no rc at all, `edit .` where the editor creates `./.envrc` → allowed
  (found RC went from none → `./.envrc`).

---

## 4. `direnv log (--status|--error) <message>`

Argument rules (checked in this order):

1. Exactly 2 arguments required (after `log`); otherwise
   `ESC[31mdirenv: error invalid argumentsESC[0m\n`, exit 1.
   (`log`, `log ""`, `log hello`, `log --status`, `log --status a b` all → this error.)
2. Argument 1 must be exactly `--status`, `-status`, `--error`, or `-error`
   (single-dash variants accepted; `status`, `--STATUS`, `---status`, `--`,
   `--status=x` rejected). Otherwise:
   `ESC[31mdirenv: error invalid log-type '<arg>'ESC[0m\n`, exit 1.
3. Argument 2 is the message, printed **verbatim** (embedded newlines/tabs/unicode pass
   through; empty string allowed).

Output (stderr only, stdout always empty, exit 0):

- `log --status hello` → `ESC[0mdirenv: hello\n`
- `log --error hello` → `ESC[31mdirenv: helloESC[0m\n`
- `log --status ""` → `ESC[0mdirenv: \n` ; `log --error ""` → `ESC[31mdirenv: ESC[0m\n`
- Multi-line: `log --status $'line1\nline2'` → `ESC[0mdirenv: line1\nline2\n`

### Interaction with `[global] log_format` / `log_filter` (see §6)

These knobs apply **only to `--status`**; `--error` always uses the default
`direnv: %s` format and is never filtered:

- Default status format is `direnv: %s`. `log_format = "CUSTOM:%s"` →
  `ESC[0mCUSTOM:hi\n`. `log_format = "-"` → status message suppressed entirely
  (zero bytes). `log_format = ""` → treated as unset (default used).
- The format string is applied **twice** through Go's `fmt.Sprintf`:
  output = `Sprintf(Sprintf(log_format, msg))` + `\n`. With a format lacking `%s`
  this produces Go's `%!`-artifacts, e.g. `log_format = "no-percent"` yields exactly
  `ESC[0mno-percent\n%!!(MISSING)(EXTRA string=hi)\n`, and `log_format = "%s %s"`
  yields `ESC[0mhi %!!(MISSING)s(MISSING)\n`.
- `log_filter` is a **keep-only** regexp on the formatted status message (not a
  drop filter): `log_filter = "hi"` keeps `hi there` (prints) and suppresses `bye`.
  Errors are unaffected (`log --error bye` still prints).
- Invalid regexp: each status-log attempt prints
  `ESC[31mdirenv: error error in log filter: error parsing regexp: missing closing ]: \`[\`ESC[0m\n`
  (for filter `[`) — note the doubled `error error in`.

---

## 5. `direnv fetchurl <url> [<integrity-hash>]`

Fetches a URL into a content-addressed store (CAS).

### CAS layout

- Directory: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/direnv/cas/` (created `0755`; if `XDG_CACHE_HOME` unset or
  empty: `$HOME/.cache/direnv/cas/`).
- File name: the **lowercase hex** encoding of the hash digest (NOT the SRI/base64 form
  shown in the man page — the man page is outdated). For sha256: 64 hex chars, e.g.
  `…/cas/23e4ca4c602ddb27746ab41722b4dfa5466299d4afe2634943254a5a29c5e485`.
- Cached files are mode **`0500`** (`r-x------`): read-only + executable for owner.
- Downloads go to a temp file `…/cas/tmp<random-number>` which is renamed into place.

### Mode 1: URL only — discover the hash

- Always performs an HTTP GET (even if the content is already in the CAS).
- Computes the **sha256** of the response body. If the CAS file for it does not exist,
  it is stored (rename, mode 0500); if it exists, nothing is stored.
- stdout when **not a tty** (piped/redirected): exactly `sha256-<base64std-padded>\n`, e.g.
  `sha256-I+TKTGAt2yd0arQXIrTfpUZimdSv4mNJQyVKWinF5IU=\n`
- stdout when **a tty** (human-readable, `\n` line endings):
  ```
  Found hash: sha256-<hash>

  Invoke fetchurl again with the hash as an argument to get the disk location:

    direnv fetchurl "<url>" "sha256-<hash>"
    #=> <absolute-cas-path>
  ```
- stderr: on a fresh store-into-CAS, two quirky warnings are printed (plain text, no
  colors/prefix; tmp name varies):
  ```
  Warning: failed to close temp file: close <casdir>/tmp<num>: file already closed
  Warning: failed to remove temp file <casdir>/tmp<num>: remove <casdir>/tmp<num>: no such file or directory
  ```
  On a cache-warm URL-only call, no warnings. Exit 0.

### Mode 2: URL + integrity hash

- Hash syntax: `<algo>-<base64>` (SRI-like). Algo `sha256`, `sha384`, `sha512` parse;
  anything else → `ESC[31mdirenv: error sri: unsupported algo <algo>ESC[0m\n`, exit 1
  (observed for `md5`, `sha1`). A string without `-` →
  `ESC[31mdirenv: error sri: not a hash <arg>ESC[0m\n`, exit 1. Standard padded base64
  required: malformed → e.g. `ESC[31mdirenv: error illegal base64 data at input byte 0ESC[0m\n`
  (byte offset varies), exit 1.
- **Cache check first**: if `<casdir>/<hex-of-given-hash-digest>` exists, the path is
  printed and the command exits 0 — **no network request and no content verification**
  (verified: pre-seeding the file with wrong content still succeeds; a `sha384-…` hash
  can only ever succeed this way, since the downloaded digest is always sha256).
- Otherwise: HTTP GET, compute **sha256** of the body, compare against the given hash
  (as full `algo-base64` strings):
  - match → store in CAS (rename + the two temp-file warnings), stdout =
    `<absolute-cas-path>\n`, exit 0.
  - mismatch → nothing stored, stdout empty, exit 1:
    `ESC[31mdirenv: error hash mismatch. Expected '<given-hash>' but got 'sha256-<actual>'ESC[0m\n`
    (e.g. `Expected 'sha256-' but got …` for an empty-digest hash; a `sha512-…` or
    `sha384-…` given hash always mismatches because "got" is always `sha256-…`).
- Extra arguments are ignored.

### HTTP behavior / errors (all exit 1, stdout empty, `ESC[31mdirenv: error …ESC[0m\n`)

- Missing URL: `… error missing URL argument …`
- Redirects (301 etc.) are followed (verified: `/subdir` → 301 → `/subdir/` → 200).
- Non-200 final status: `… error expected status code 200 but got 404 …`
- Bad URL `notaurl`: `… error Get "notaurl": unsupported protocol scheme "" …`
- Bad URL `://bad`: `… error parse "://bad": missing protocol scheme …`
- `ftp://…`: `… error Get "ftp://example.com/x": unsupported protocol scheme "ftp" …`
- Connection refused (server down): `… error Get "<url>": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:<port>: connect: connection refused …`
  — note a warm cache still errors **if the URL is fetched**; but in URL+hash mode a
  cache hit never touches the network, so it succeeds with the server down.

---

## 6. Configuration file loading

### Locations and precedence

- Config directory = `$DIRENV_CONFIG` if that env var is **non-empty**, else
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/direnv` if `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` non-empty, else `$HOME/.config/direnv`.
  - `DIRENV_CONFIG` pointing to a nonexistent directory, or to a regular file, is
    treated as "no config" silently (no error).
  - If no config directory can be determined at all (HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME both
    unset), commands that need the config fail with
    `ESC[31mdirenv: error couldn't find a configuration directory for direnvESC[0m\n`,
    exit 1 (observed for `status`, `edit`, `log`; `version` still works, exit 0).
- Inside the config directory, the file **`direnv.toml`** is read. If `direnv.toml`
  does not exist, the legacy **`config.toml`** is read instead. If **both** exist,
  `direnv.toml` wins completely (verified: whitelist in `config.toml` ignored when a
  `direnv.toml` without whitelist is present). If neither exists, defaults are used
  silently.
- Unknown TOML sections/keys are ignored (exit 0).
- Malformed TOML, or type mismatches, abort the whole command: stdout empty, exit 1:
  - `ESC[31mdirenv: error LoadConfig() failed to parse <path>: toml: line 2: expected '.' or ']' to end table name, but got '\n' insteadESC[0m\n` (for `[whitelist` + `prefix = [`)
  - `ESC[31mdirenv: error LoadConfig() failed to parse <path>: toml: line 2 (last key "whitelist.prefix"): incompatible types: TOML value has type string; destination has type sliceESC[0m\n` (for `prefix = "..."` instead of an array; same for `prefix = [ 123 ]` with type int)
  - `ESC[31mdirenv: error LoadConfig() failed to parse <path>: toml: line 1 (last key "x"): expected value but found '\n' insteadESC[0m\n` (for `x = `)
  (Error text is from the pelletier/go-toml v2 parser.)

### `[whitelist]` — implicit allow

`prefix` and `exact` each accept an array of strings. A whitelisted `.envrc` is loaded
by `direnv export <shell>` (and other loading commands) **without `direnv allow`** —
verified: export exits 0 and emits the usual status lines
(`ESC[0mdirenv: loading <path>\n`, `ESC[0mdirenv: export +VAR\n`).
Without whitelist/allow the same export exits 1 with stdout still containing the
`DIRENV_*` export statements and stderr:
`ESC[31mdirenv: error <abspath>/.envrc is blocked. Run \`direnv allow\` to approve its contentESC[0m\n`.

Tilde expansion: an entry starting with `~/` has the `~` replaced by `$HOME`
(`~/wlproj`, `~/`, `~/wlproj/.envrc` all work). A bare `~` is NOT expanded.

`prefix` — **pure string-prefix match** on the `.envrc`'s absolute path (after tilde
expansion). No path cleaning, no component awareness:

- `prefix = ["/tmp/probe_misc/wl"]` allows `/tmp/probe_misc/wl/proj/.envrc` **and also**
  `/tmp/probe_misc/wl2/proj/.envrc` (shares the string prefix!).
- Partial components match: `prefix = ["/tmp/probe_misc/w"]` allows `…/wl/proj/.envrc`.
- Trailing slash is fine (`…/wl/` matches).
- Double slashes do NOT match (`/tmp//probe_misc//wl` ≠ the real path).
- Relative entries never match (paths compared are absolute).
- `prefix = [""]` matches everything.

`exact` — exact string match after normalization:

- An entry that is a directory path is treated as `<entry>/.envrc`
  (docs; verified: `exact = ["/tmp/probe_misc/wl/proj"]` allows exactly
  `/tmp/probe_misc/wl/proj/.envrc`).
- A full file path (`…/proj/.envrc`) also works. A trailing slash on a directory entry
  still works (`…/proj/`), but a trailing slash on a file entry (`…/proj/.envrc/`)
  does NOT match.
- Does not extend to nested directories: with `exact = ["…/wl/proj"]`,
  `…/wl/proj/nested/.envrc` is still blocked.
- Non-matching paths are simply blocked (no error).

### `[global] log_format` / `log_filter`

Covered in §4 (they affect status logging, incl. `direnv log --status`; defaults:
`log_format = "direnv: %s"`, no filter; `log_format = "-"` disables status logs).

---

## 7. Things I could NOT determine

1. `version` comparison of two- vs three-part equality (`2.37` vs `2.37.0`) — untestable
   with a fixed binary version of 2.37.1; assumed `golang.org/x/mod/semver` semantics.
2. The exact set/order of fallback editors beyond what PATH probing revealed
   (`editor > subl > nano > vim > emacs`); an exotic default editor present on some
   other system can't be ruled out, but these five are the complete accepted set among
   15 common names tested.
3. fetchurl with `sha384`/`sha512` given hashes: the cache-hit filename uses the hex of
   the given digest, but a cache *miss* can never succeed (computed digest is always
   sha256, so the string comparison always fails) — whether this is intentional or a
   bug is not observable.
4. Whether the two fetchurl temp-file warnings (close/remove) are version- or
   OS-dependent; observed consistently on this Linux ext4-ish /tmp.
5. `log_filter` matching is applied to the formatted message string; whether it also
   sees the `direnv: ` prefix or ANSI bytes was not fully pinned down (filter `hi`
   matched message `hi there`; filter on the prefix text was not tested).

payload.resultSummary:
Task complete. Specification written to **`/workspace/reference/specs/misc-config.md`** (~21 KB). All probing was black-box CLI only, in an isolated `HOME=/tmp/probe_misc/home` with XDG dirs pointed inside it; exact bytes were captured with `od -c`, and stdout/stderr/exit code were recorded separately for every case. The local `python3 -m http.server` used for fetchurl probes was killed afterwards.

Key findings per assigned topic:

1. **`version`**: no-arg prints exactly `2.37.1\n` (exit 0). With an arg it validates via `golang.org/x/mod/semver` semantics (leading `v` auto-prepended; 1–3 numeric parts, no leading zeros, prerelease/build rules) and exits 0 iff `v2.37.1 >= arg`. Exact error strings documented: `v<arg> is not a valid semver version` and `current version v2.37.1 is older than the desired version v<arg>`, both wrapped in `\x1b[31m…\x1b[0m`. ~30 comparison cases tabulated.

2. **`help`/no-args/unknown**: `direnv` and `direnv help` print public help (exit 0) matching `assets/help.txt` except the "Supported SHELL values" line whose 12 shell names are **randomly ordered each run** (Go map iteration). Any non-empty arg to `help` (even `false`/`garbage`) prints the private help. Unknown command: empty stdout, `command "<argv0> <cmd>" not found`, exit 1 — only argv0+argv1 appear.

3. **`edit`**: dir arg → appends `/.envrc`; other args verbatim; no-arg searches upward (absolute path). `$VISUAL` ignored; fallback editor search order `editor > subl > nano > vim > emacs` (vi/nvim NOT included). Editor is run as `bash -c '<EDITOR> <ANSI-C-quoted-path>'` (shell-interpreted, spaces safe). **Auto-allow quirk**: allow happens iff the *found RC for CWD* changed (mtime/appearance/deletion) during editing — then the *edited* file is allowed; editing a non-CWD rc without touching the found rc does NOT allow it.

4. **`log`**: requires exactly 2 args; type must be `--status`/`-status`/`--error`/`-error` else `invalid log-type '<arg>'`; wrong arity → `invalid arguments`. Status format `\x1b[0mdirenv: <msg>\n`, error `\x1b[31mdirenv: <msg>\x1b[0m\n`, colors unconditional (tty/pipe/TERM=dumb identical). `log_format` is applied **twice** through `fmt.Sprintf` (verified against real Go output), `-` suppresses status only; `log_filter` is a keep-only regexp on the raw message; errors bypass both.

5. **`fetchurl`**: CAS at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/direnv/cas/<lowercase-hex-digest>` (man page's base64url filename is outdated), files mode **0500**. URL-only always downloads, prints `sha256-<b64>\n` piped / "Found hash:…" block on tty; fresh stores emit two `Warning: failed to close/remove temp file…` lines. URL+hash: pure existence cache-hit (no network, no content verification), else downloads and compares against always-sha256 digest — so sha384/sha512 given hashes can only succeed via pre-seeded cache. Exact errors for mismatch, `sri: unsupported algo md5`, `sri: not a hash <x>`, base64 errors, 404 (`expected status code 200 but got 404`), bad URLs, connection refused; redirects followed; extra args ignored.

6. **Config**: `DIRENV_CONFIG` > `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/direnv` > `~/.config/direnv`; `direnv.toml` beats legacy `config.toml` when both exist (legacy still honored alone). Malformed TOML → `LoadConfig() failed to parse <path>: toml: …` (go-toml v2 messages), exit 1. No HOME → `couldn't find a configuration directory for direnv`. Whitelist: `prefix` is a **raw string-prefix** match (partial components match, `""` matches all, double slashes don't, `~/` expands but bare `~` doesn't); `exact` matches dir (=dir+`/.envrc`) or file path exactly, no nesting. Whitelisted envrc loads via `export` without `allow` (verified); blocked case's exact error recorded.

Known-unknowns are listed in §7 of the spec (e.g. two- vs three-part semver equality untestable with a fixed binary version).

Exact error strings documented: `v<arg> is not a valid semver version` and `current version v2.37.1 is older than the desired version v<arg>`, both wrapped in `\x1b[31m…\x1b[0m`. ~30 comparison cases tabulated.

2. **`help`/no-args/unknown**: `direnv` and `direnv help` print public help (exit 0) matching `assets/help.txt` except the "Supported SHELL values" line whose 12 shell names are **randomly ordered each run** (Go map iteration). 3. **`edit`**: dir arg → appends `/.envrc`; other args verbatim; no-arg searches upward (absolute path). `$VISUAL` ignored; fallback editor search order `editor > subl > nano > vim > emacs` (vi/nvim NOT included). Editor is run as `bash -c '<EDITOR> <ANSI-C-quoted-path>'` (shell-interpreted, spaces safe). **Auto-allow quirk**: allow happens iff the *found RC for CWD* changed (mtime/appearance/deletion) during editing — then the *edited* file is allowed; editing a non-CWD rc without touching the found rc does NOT allow it.

4. **`log`**: requires exactly 2 args; type must be `--status`/`-status`/`--error`/`-error` else `invalid log-type '<arg>'`; wrong arity → `invalid arguments`. Status format `\x1b[0mdirenv: <msg>\n`, error `\x1b[31mdirenv: <msg>\x1b[0m\n`, colors unconditional (tty/pipe/TERM=dumb identical). `log_format` is applied **twice** through `fmt.Sprintf` (verified against real Go output), `-` suppresses status only; `log_filter` is a keep-only regexp on the raw message; errors bypass both.

URL-only always downloads, prints `sha256-<b64>\n` piped / "Found hash:…" block on tty; fresh stores emit two `Warning: failed to close/remove temp file…` lines. URL+hash: pure existence cache-hit (no network, no content verification), else downloads and compares against always-sha256 digest — so sha384/sha512 given hashes can only succeed via pre-seeded cache. Exact errors for mismatch, `sri: unsupported algo md5`, `sri: not a hash <x>`, base64 errors, 404 (`expected status code 200 but got 404`), bad URLs, connection refused; redirects followed; extra args ignored.

Whitelist: `prefix` is a **raw string-prefix** match (partial components match, `""` matches all, double slashes don't, `~/` expands but bare `~` doesn't); `exact` matches dir (=dir+`/.envrc`) or file path exactly, no nesting.
